content.value_statement: Large agent instruction files waste context and hide important rules. This skill splits them into a compact root file and focused linked documents.
actual_capabilities: Finds contradictory instructions before restructuring begins.
Separates universal root guidance from topic-specific details.
Groups remaining guidance into focused files such as testing, code style, and architecture.
Provides templates for a minimal root file and linked instruction files.
Flags redundant, vague, obvious, or outdated instructions for deletion.
Checks that links, coverage, consistency, and file scope remain clear.
limitations: It needs the existing instruction file content to produce useful results.
It asks the user to resolve contradictions before continuing.
It does not prove that every project convention is correct.
It may need adjustment for unusual repository layouts or agent tools.

use_cases.title: Clean Up CLAUDE.md
use_cases.description: Turn a long CLAUDE.md file into a short root guide with linked topic files.

use_cases.title: Organize AGENTS.md
use_cases.description: Group mixed coding, testing, style, and workflow rules into maintainable documents.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidance
use_cases.description: Create a consistent structure for agent instructions across multiple repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single instruction file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my CLAUDE.md using progressive disclosure. Keep only universal guidance in the root file.

prompt_templates.title: Split By Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AGENTS.md and split it into focused linked files for testing, style, architecture, and workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Conflicts First
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my agent instructions for contradictions first. Ask me to resolve conflicts before you restructure the files.

prompt_templates.title: Audit And Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a careful cleanup plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit all agent instruction files in this repository. Propose a minimal root file, linked topics, deletion candidates, and verification checks.

output_examples.input: A 300-line CLAUDE.md mixes project overview, testing rules, style rules, and workflow notes.
output: A short root file keeps the project summary and essential commands.
Linked topic files hold testing, style, architecture, and workflow guidance.
A deletion report lists vague or redundant instructions.

output_examples.input: An AGENTS.md file contains conflicting style rules and repeated testing guidance.
output: The skill reports the conflicting rules and asks which one should win.
After resolution, it groups the remaining guidance into clear topic files.
The final checklist verifies links, coverage, and root file size.

output_examples.input: A team wants one structure for agent instructions across several repositories.
output: Each repository receives the same root file pattern and topic categories.
Project-specific exceptions stay in the relevant linked files.
Teams can compare guidance without reading one large file.

best_practices: Start from a clean git state so changes are easy to review.
Resolve contradictions before moving content into linked files.
Keep the root file limited to guidance needed for every task.
anti_patterns: Keeping every project rule in the root instruction file.
Creating many small files that make guidance harder to find.
Preserving vague instructions that do not change agent behavior.

faq.question: What files does this skill help refactor?
faq.answer: It targets AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, COPILOT.md, and similar agent instruction files.

faq.question: Does it delete instructions automatically?
faq.answer: It flags deletion candidates and explains why they may be removed. The user should review them.

faq.question: Can it handle conflicting rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies contradictions and asks the user to choose the correct rule before restructuring.

faq.question: What should stay in the root file?
faq.answer: Keep the project summary, nonstandard commands, critical overrides, and rules that apply to every task.

faq.question: How many linked files should I create?
faq.answer: The skill recommends three to eight focused files for most projects.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The structure is useful for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and similar coding agents.
